messages:
maria: quick heads-up: zephyr-mini int4 bringup in staging looks ok overall but portuguese recall@1 tanked and embeddings form a single razor cluster. curious if anyones seen int4 cause language-specific norm collapse.

omar: can you drop the eval summary + dataset?

maria: using multilingual-holdout-v4 (en/es/pt/fr), 60k corpus, stratified queries. snippet:```
model: zephyr-mini
quant: int4 per-channel
seq_len: 128
metrics: {
  "recall@1": {"en": 0.82, "es": 0.80, "pt": 0.64, "fr": 0.79},
  "recall@5": {"en": 0.94, "es": 0.92, "pt": 0.84, "fr": 0.91}
}
cluster_summary: {"pt": {"clusters": 1, "largest_frac": 0.78, "mean_pairwise_cos": 0.91}}
```

julian: 0.91 mean_pairwise_cos for pt is alarmingly high. Did you run FP16 baseline?

maria: yes fp16: pt recall@1 0.79, mean_pairwise_cos 0.72. so quant shift +0.19 cosine.

sara: might be quant-induced saturation of certain dims. can you print per-dim variance before/after quant for pt examples vs en?

maria: ran variance diff, quick table:```
per_dim_var_ratio_mean: {"pt": 0.42, "en": 0.89}
num_dims_near_zero_pt: 128 -> 54 dims with var < 1e-6
```
so PT dims collapsed.

omar: could be tokenizer merging: portuguese has more contracted tokens (e.g., do+o), check token distribution and vocab ids frequency. also check whether calibration used layerwise symmetric vs asymmetric.

maria: token stats:```
most_common_tokens_pt: ["de", "que", "do", "na", "para"]
avg_token_tokens_pt: 3.7
```
calibration: symmetric per-channel minmax clip with 99.9 percentile.

julian: try two quick mitigations: 1) per-language clipping (run calibration on PT subset only) 2) small bias-add (learned per-dim add) post-quant to restore variance. Also test per-tensor int4 to see if per-channel quant exacerbated.

maria: queued runs: per-tensor int4 and pt-only calibration. cmd:```
./run_eval.sh --model zephyr-mini --quant int4 --mode per-tensor --dataset multilingual-holdout-v4 --subset pt --out /tmp/zephyr_pt_ptensor.json
```

ops-bot: cluster-job queued (job id zk-1122) 1 GPUs, ETA ~9m

maria: results: per-tensor int4 improved pt recall@1 to 0.70 (was 0.64), mean_pairwise_cos 0.79, largest_frac 0.51. pt-only calibration + asymmetric clipping got recall@1 0.74, mean_pairwise_cos 0.76.

sara: good. suggests per-channel minmax over multilingual calibration biased the scale for pt. per-tensor smoothing helps. For longer-term, we should add a calibration step per-language for multilingual models or a mixed calibration schedule.

julian: agree. also add automated regression: when deploying quant variants, run small per-lang cluster-check: compute largest_cluster_frac and mean_pairwise_cosine per-lang; fail if largest_frac>0.6 or mean_cos>0.85.

maria: capturing failure examples for product review. will upload 15 query->nearest pairs. also trying a cheap post-quant per-dim white-noise injection (sigma=1e-3) to un-stagnate dead dims, testing now.

omar: also re-run subset on older kernel stack (A100 runtime vs gk5 runtime) to rule out numerics. in my past cases kernel rounding + int4 often interacts with fused attention reorder.

maria: scheduled kernel comparison. ops-bot: job zk-1122 finished, artifacts: /artifacts/zk-1122/zephyr_int4_pt.json

sara: follow-ups: 1) doc add `quant-calibration-guidelines.md` with per-lang option 2) add unit smoke that runs small multilingual holdout and checks cluster metrics 3) decide default quant mode for multilingual models (probably per-tensor for int4 for now)

maria: filing ticket: https://redwood.internal/t/ML-1608 with artifacts and sample failures. assigning to eng-ml. :thumbsup:
